standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice calendar basics. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Before explicit calendar instruction, the learner is given a real family calendar (paper or provided) or a provided sample and attempts, on their own, to answer three questions about it: today's date, one upcoming event, and the number of days until it.
safetyNotes: Calendar entries stay general (event name and date); no private family detail is required beyond what's already on the calendar.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real family calendar is available, the learner instead uses a provided printed or digital sample calendar with sample events to find today's date, one event, and the day-count the same way.

materials: adult-or-local: a real or provided calendar

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Was your warm-up guess close to the actual day-count? What made counting on the real calendar easier or harder than guessing?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Calendar reading accuracy: Finds today's date and a real event correctly. | Day-count accuracy: Count is exact or off by one. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Find two upcoming events instead of one and compare which is sooner, explaining how they determined that from the calendar.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice calendar basics. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: a real or provided calendar
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: calendar basics worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Before explicit calendar instruction, the learner is given a real family calendar (paper or provided) or a provided sample and attempts, on their own, to answer three questions about it: today's date, one upcoming event, and the number of days until it.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact calendar basics decision or action.
Model move 2: Before looking at the calendar, guess: how many days until the next event you already know is coming up?
Model move 3: Using the calendar, find today's date, one upcoming event within the next two weeks, and count the days until that event.
Model check: Calendar reading accuracy: Finds today's date and a real event correctly. | Day-count accuracy: Count is exact or off by one.

resources.title: calendar basics action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for calendar basics.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: calendar basics coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Before explicit calendar instruction, the learner is given a real family calendar (paper or provided) or a provided sample and attempts, on their own, to answer three questions about it: today's date, one upcoming event, and the number of days until it.
Coach direction: Before looking at the calendar, guess: how many days until the next event you already know is coming up?
Learner prompt: State your guess.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: calendar basics complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Using the calendar, find today's date, one upcoming event within the next two weeks, and count the days until that event.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Write today’s date, the event you found, and how many days away it is.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My day-count matches what the calendar actually shows, checked by counting the boxes or days myself.

Equal-access rule: If no real family calendar is available, the learner instead uses a provided printed or digital sample calendar with sample events to find today's date, one event, and the day-count the same way.

resources.title: calendar basics minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Was your warm-up guess close to the actual day-count? What made counting on the real calendar easier or harder than guessing?
Success checks: Calendar reading accuracy: Finds today's date and a real event correctly. | Day-count accuracy: Count is exact or off by one.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: calendar basics supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional calendar basics condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.
Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Calendar reading accuracy: Finds today's date and a real event correctly. | Day-count accuracy: Count is exact or off by one..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
